title: IGF2BP3 promotes M2 macrophage polarization and ESCC progression by increasing USP36-mediated β-catenin stabilization.
abstract: Esophageal squamous cell carcinoma is a highly aggressive malignancy with poor prognosis that is characterized by an immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment that critically contributes to tumor progression and therapeutic resistance. RNA-binding proteins are emerging regulators of cancer biology; however, their role in shaping the tumor immune microenvironment of esophageal squamous cell carcinoma remains largely unexplored. This study aimed to investigate the function and mechanism of the RNA-binding protein IGF2BP3 in esophageal squamous cell carcinoma progression and immune modulation. Single-cell RNA sequencing datasets including esophageal squamous cell carcinoma and adjacent normal tissues were integrated to identify dysregulated RNA-binding proteins. The functional role of IGF2BP3 was evaluated using in vitro assays, organoid models, and immunocompetent and immunodeficient mouse models. RNA immunoprecipitation, polysome profiling, ubiquitination assays, and luciferase reporter assays were employed to elucidate the underlying molecular mechanisms. Immune cell infiltration was analyzed by flow cytometry, immunohistochemistry, and multiplex immunofluorescence. Virtual screening, biolayer interferometry, and molecular docking were used to identify small-molecule inhibitors of IGF2BP3. Statistical analyses included Student's t tests, one-way analysis of variance, Kaplan‒Meier survival analysis, and correlation analyses. IGF2BP3 was specifically overexpressed in epithelial tumor cells, exhibited progressively increasing expression during esophageal squamous cell carcinoma progression, and correlated with poor clinical outcomes. IGF2BP3 promoted tumor growth by activating Wnt signaling through the stabilization of β-catenin. Mechanistically, IGF2BP3 increased the translation of the deubiquitinase USP36 without altering the stability of its messenger RNA, leading to the USP36-mediated deubiquitination and stabilization of β-catenin. Activation of β-catenin signaling increased the transcription and secretion of transforming growth factor beta, which promoted the polarization of macrophages toward the immunosuppressive M2 phenotype. Pharmacological inhibition of IGF2BP3 with digoxin disrupted the IGF2BP3-USP36-β-catenin axis, reduced transforming growth factor beta production, suppressed tumor growth, and increased the efficacy of paclitaxel and PD-1 blockade in preclinical models. This study identifies IGF2BP3 as a critical posttranscriptional regulator that links oncogenic signaling to immune suppression in esophageal squamous cell carcinoma. Targeting IGF2BP3 represents a promising therapeutic strategy to remodel the tumor microenvironment and improve responses to chemotherapy and immunotherapy.

title: Silscore: modelling siRNA potency with positional thermodynamics and data-selected nucleotide-identity terms
abstract: Small interfering RNAs (siRNAs) enable programmable gene silencing, but candidates targeting the same transcript can differ markedly in potency. Existing predictors range from interpretable empirical rules with limited accuracy to high-capacity models that can lose performance when datasets or targets change. We present Silscore, a guide-only model that combines a quadratic preference for overall duplex stability, a position-resolved profile of nearest-neighbour stacking energies and sparse nucleotide-identity terms selected from residuals left unexplained by thermodynamics. Its main fit uses 26 parameters, fewer than half as many as any trainable comparator evaluated here. We evaluate Silscore on the canonical split of the Huesken dataset, two external datasets (Mixset and Katoh-Suzuki), and an evaluation in which the same guides are tested after training on dissimilar targets. Silscore attains the highest observed Pearson correlation in all three transfer evaluations, and the data support an advantage over every applicable comparator on Katoh-Suzuki. For a fixed evaluation set, we compare two equally sized training sets with higher or lower sequence similarity to the evaluation sequences. After training on the less similar sequences, Silscore has the highest observed correlation, and the data do not establish a change in its performance. The fitted parameters can also be interpreted directly: identity terms locate sequence effects that base-pairing energies cannot express, global stability has a data-estimated intermediate optimum, and local energy profiles recover terminal asymmetry and a preference for weaker seed and stronger central pairing. Silscore thus provides a compact, data-driven model that combines strong predictive performance with robustness when tested in new settings and expresses previously reported empirical preferences as quantities estimated from data.

title: Time-Resolved Proteomics of a Polyglutamine-Expanded Huntingtin in vitro Cell Model Reveals Early RNA-Regulatory Compensation and Late Respiratory-Chain Remodeling
abstract: Huntington disease (HD) is caused by a polyglutamine-expanded huntingtin protein that exerts progressive cellular toxicity. However, the temporal order of pathogenic events, and in particular which changes arise early and which emerge late, remains incompletely defined, despite their distinct therapeutic implications. To examine this trajectory, we profiled the proteome of a huntingtin-expressing cell model at early (72 h) and late (144 h) stages. Rather than a linear progression, the proteome changed in two distinct stages. At the early stage, cells showed increased abundance of RNA-processing, splicing, and protein-synthesis proteins, which may reflect an adaptive response to preserve gene-expression fidelity under stress. By the late stage, many of these proteins were depleted and mitochondrial energy-metabolism proteins dominated the response. Notably, 85% of proteins altered at both time points reversed direction between stages (95% at a false-discovery rate below 5%), and all reversals were supported by a significant genotype-by-time interaction, indicating that mutant huntingtin reorganizes the proteome rather than amplifying a fixed set of perturbations. Subunit-level analysis of the respiratory chain showed that Complex IV and ATP synthase subunits were reduced at 72 h, whereas at 144 h subunits of all five complexes were broadly increased, most strongly in Complex I and III, with a few distal subunits (COX5B, ATP5F1A, ATP5F1B) remaining reduced. Leveraging this proteomic map, we applied an AI-assisted, direction-aware drug repurposing strategy. Of 1,712 differentially abundant proteins, 498 were druggable, 109 had at least one agent whose mechanism was concordant with the required correction, and 89 of these 109 proteins mapped to at least one agent listed as approved in the source databases (56 to an agent with current regulatory approval). These included the approved Complex I inhibitor metformin, the investigational Complex I inhibitor ME-344, and pathway-level mitochondria-directed agents (elamipretide/SS-31, approved only for Barth syndrome; MitoQ, a dietary supplement), several of which have previously been evaluated in HD models. Collectively, these findings describe a two-stage proteomic response to mutant huntingtin in this cell model and suggest a putative early window for preclinical intervention testing, before late respiratory-chain remodeling is established.

title: METTL1-regulated tRF-5001b suppresses lung adenocarcinoma by impairing QARS1 interaction with tRNAGln and inhibiting HMGA2 translation.
abstract: Lung adenocarcinoma (LUAD) remains the leading cause of cancer-related mortality worldwide, yet the impacts of tRNA-derived fragments (tRFs) on its progression are not fully understood. This study aimed to investigate the role of tRF-5001b in LUAD. The expression of tRF-5001b in LUAD tissues was analyzed using public datasets and validated by Northern blotting. The biological functions of tRF-5001b, QARS1, and HMGA2 were evaluated using EdU, transwell, and CCK-8 assays in vitro, as well as subcutaneous and intravenous injection models in vivo. RNA fluorescence in situ hybridization and immunofluorescence were performed to determine the subcellular localization of tRF-5001b and QARS1. The expression levels of METTL1, WDR4, QARS1, and HMGA2 were examined by qRT-PCR and Western blotting. RNA immunoprecipitation, RNA pull-down, silver staining, co-immunoprecipitation, and molecular docking were conducted to investigate the interaction between tRF-5001b and QARS1. Puromycin incorporation assays were performed to assess the effect of tRF-5001b on global protein translation. tRF-5001b was significantly downregulated in LUAD tissues and exhibited tumor-suppressive effects by inhibiting tumor cell proliferation, migration, and invasion both in vitro and in vivo. Mechanistically, tRF-5001b competitively disrupted the interaction between QARS1 and tRNAGln, thereby suppressing HMGA2 translation and attenuating LUAD progression. Furthermore, METTL1 was identified as a negative regulator of tRF-5001b biogenesis through catalyzing m7G modification of tRNA-Tyr-GTA. This study identifies tRF-5001b as a suppressor of LUAD progression through inhibition of HMGA2 translation and highlights METTL1 as a key regulator of its biogenesis. These findings provide new insights into tRF-mediated molecular mechanisms and suggest potential therapeutic targets for lung adenocarcinoma.

title: Paternal exposure to decabromodiphenyl ethane (DBDPE) accelerates aging in offspring mice: Intergenerational effects and underlying mechanisms.
abstract: Decabromodiphenyl ethane (DBDPE), an emerging brominated flame retardant widely used as a replacement for legacy flame retardants, is persistent in the environment and increasingly detected in humans. However, whether long-term DBDPE exposure impairs male reproductive function and consequently affects offspring health remains largely unknown. Here, male mice were orally exposed to DBDPE (0, 0.01, 0.1, 1, and 10 mg/kg body weight/day) for 6 months. Chronic DBDPE exposure resulted in dose-dependent testicular accumulation, impaired sperm quality, and reduced fertilization capacity. Paternal DBDPE exposure also induced aging-like pathological alterations and shortened lifespan in F1 offspring. Sperm small non-coding RNA sequencing identified marked alterations in the sperm PIWI-interacting RNA (piRNA) profile, including increased abundance of the database-annotated piRNA piR-001169. Mechanistically, piR-001169 suppressed ten-eleven translocation 3 (Tet3) expression during early embryonic development, leading to increased methylation of the heat shock protein family A member 1 A (Hspa1a) and Hspa1b promoters and reduced heat shock protein 70 (Hsp70) expression in multiple offspring tissues. This dysregulation of the Hsp70/proteostasis axis was accompanied by increased protein aggregation and aging-related tissue injury. Restoration of Hsp70 expression partially ameliorated proteostasis disruption and aging-related pathological changes, supporting a functional role of impaired Hsp70-dependent proteostasis in the offspring phenotype. Notably, the aging-related phenotypes observed in F1 offspring were not detectable in F2 offspring. Collectively, these findings demonstrate that chronic paternal DBDPE exposure impairs male reproductive function and induces aging-like phenotypes in F1 offspring, with sperm piR-001169-Tet3 regulation and subsequent disruption of Hsp70-dependent proteostasis representing a potential paternal epigenetic mechanism.

title: Intelligent Modular Dual-Readout Architecture Driven by CRISPR/Cas13a-CHA Cascade and Machine Learning for Portable Multiplex MicroRNA Liquid Biopsy in Early Lung Cancer.
abstract: Precise detection of trace miRNAs in liquid biopsies is critical for early lung cancer screening, yet current methods are frequently limited by complex reverse transcription procedures and potential enzymatic amplification biases. Herein, we developed a sequencing-free and highly portable dual-mode biosensing platform for decentralized clinical diagnostics by synergizing highly specific CRISPR/Cas13a recognition with exponential non-enzymatic catalytic hairpin assembly amplification (CHA). Trace target miRNAs activate Cas13a to trans-cleave the RNA trigger strand, while intact RNA triggers can precisely initiate downstream assembly networks. The Cas13a molecular lock completely eliminates spontaneous hairpin crosslinking interference. Based on this mechanism, we separately constructed a fluorescence and a multiplex surface-enhanced Raman scattering biosensing platform. The catalytic network drives reporter-embedded bimetallic nanoparticles to specifically bind plasmonic chips, forming sandwich resonance structures for absolute multiplex spectral quantification. The system synchronously processes and analyzes four lung cancer-associated miRNAs within 80 min, achieving an ultralow attomolar diagnostic limit and an exceptionally broad linear dynamic range spanning ten orders of magnitude. Clinical validation using 50 plasma samples demonstrated high quantitative agreement with standard qRT-PCR alongside exceptional anti-interference characteristics. Integrating a machine classification model to extract spectral features successfully clustered distinct pathological stages with the accuracy of 80.00 and 93.33%, respectively. The systematic framework, merging miniature programmable biochemical cascade pathways with multidimensional artificial intelligence predictions, provides a highly powerful novel diagnostic paradigm to overcome traditional barriers in complex liquid biopsy translational applications.

title: Csi-miR-71a delivered by Clonorchis sinensis extracellular vesicles suppresses liver fibrosis by targeting Scube3 to inhibit the TGF-β/Smad and PI3K/AKT signaling pathways.
abstract: Clonorchis sinensis is a major food-borne parasite that contributes to liver fibrosis in the host by activating hepatic stellate cells (HSCs) and promoting extracellular matrix deposition. Recent studies have revealed that miRNAs carried by C. sinensis-derived extracellular vesicles (EVs) have important roles in host-parasite interactions. However, their specific functions and underlying regulatory mechanisms in liver fibrosis remain largely unclear. In this study, EVs were isolated from C. sinensis excretory-secretory products and characterized by electron microscopy, nanoparticle tracking, and western blotting. Fluorescent labeling confirmed their uptake by HSC-T6 cells, suggesting direct parasite-host communication. Small RNA sequencing of EVs and HSCs isolated from infected and uninfected mice revealed that Csi-miR-71a was significantly enriched in both EVs and infected HSCs. To investigate the function of this miRNA, synthetic mimics, inhibitors, and lentiviral vectors were used in HSC-T6 cells, primary HSCs, and mouse liver tissues. Overexpression of Csi-miR-71a suppressed fibrotic markers (α-smooth muscle actin, collagen type I, and collagen type III), whereas Csi-miR-71a inhibition had the opposite effect. In a CCl4-induced mouse model, lentiviral delivery of Csi-miR-71a alleviated liver fibrosis, as shown by reduced collagen deposition and fibrotic gene expression. Bioinformatic analyses and dual-luciferase assays identified signal peptide-CUB-EGF-like domain-containing protein 3 (Scube3) as a direct target of Csi-miR-71a, and co-immunoprecipitation confirmed the interaction with transforming growth factor (TGF)-β receptor II. Scube3 silencing reduced Smad2/3 and PI3K/AKT phosphorylation. Conversely, restoration of SCUBE3 expression in Csi-miR-71a mimic-treated HSC-T6 cells rescued fibrosis-associated protein expression and reactivated both signaling pathways, supporting SCUBE3 as a major functional mediator of Csi-miR-71a activity. These findings demonstrated that Csi-miR-71a, specifically enriched in EVs from C. sinensis, suppressed liver fibrosis by targeting Scube3 to inhibit the TGF-β/Smad and PI3K/AKT pathways. Together, these results reveal a previously unrecognized miRNA-mediated mechanism by which C. sinensis modulates host fibrosis responses, providing novel insights into parasite-host molecular crosstalk and suggesting a potential regulatory target for liver fibrosis.

title: GM-CSF and M-CSF driven differentiation differentially regulates Chikungunya virus infection and antiviral responses in human monocyte-derived macrophages.
abstract: Chikungunya virus is an arthritogenic alphavirus causing debilitating joint pain in infected individuals. The mechanisms driving CHIKV-associated arthralgia is poorly understood, however, macrophages have been implicated as potential reservoirs of persistent viral material and mediators of immunopathology. Granulocyte Macrophage-Colony Stimulating Factor (GM-CSF) and Macrophage-Colony Stimulating Factor (M-CSF) are cytokines that serve as myeloid growth factors that bias macrophages toward pro-inflammatory and anti-inflammatory phenotypes, respectively. In this study, we examined how cytokine-driven macrophage differentiation via GM-CSF and M-CSF influences susceptibility to and responses against CHIKV infection in vitro. Using parallel donor-matched cultures of primary macrophages, we show that GM-CSF-differentiated macrophages are highly permissive to CHIKV and Mayaro virus (MAYV) infection and support robust viral replication, whereas M-CSF-differentiated macrophages are resistant to CHIKV replication and lack detectable levels of viral protein expression. Despite these differences, we observed pro-inflammatory, M1-skewing of CHIKV-infected macrophages, regardless of differentiation state. Interestingly, we observe higher production of IFNα and IP10/CXCL10 in M-CSF differentiated macrophages, suggesting that M-CSF promotes an antiviral state that restricts CHIKV infection. Stimulation of macrophages with double-stranded RNA (polyinosinic:polycytidylic acid; poly(I:C)), but not with single-stranded RNA (resiquimod, R848), recapitulated the antiviral cytokine and chemokine response induced by CHIKV infection. These findings suggest that dsRNA sensing plays a more prominent role than ssRNA sensing in driving the macrophage antiviral response to CHIKV. Together, these findings highlight macrophage differentiation as a critical determinant of CHIKV susceptibility and antiviral immunity in humans, with implications for understanding inflammatory pathogenesis during infection.

title: Non-invasive Temporal Interference Stimulation of the Hippocampus Ameliorates Recognition Memory Impairments in Chronic Restraint Stress Mice.
abstract: Memory impairment in Major Depressive Disorder (MDD) leads to profound functional disability and poor clinical outcomes, yet effective non-invasive treatments specifically targeting this domain are lacking. In this study, we aimed to develop and evaluate a non‑invasive neuromodulation strategy for memory impairments in depression. Specifically, we tested whether temporal interference stimulation (TIS), a technique capable of focally modulating deep brain structures, could alleviate memory impairments in a chronic restraint stress (CRS) mouse model of depression. TIS at 40-Hz was applied to target the hippocampus. Memory performance was assessed using multiple behavioral tasks, and analyses including immunofluorescence, in vivo electrophysiology, western blot, and RNA‑sequencing were performed. We found that CRS stably induced depressive-like behaviors and impaired hippocampus-dependent memory, as evidenced by a reduced recognition index in the NOR test and decreased freezing time in the contextual FCT. These impairments coincided with hyperactivation of hippocampal inhibitory neurons and elevated gamma-band synchrony between bilateral DG regions. TIS significantly improved recognition memory, with a nonsignificant trend toward improvement in contextual fear memory, and attenuated the associated neural alterations, which shifted toward control levels. Concomitantly, TIS partially reversed CRS-induced changes in hippocampal gene expression related to synaptic function and upregulated GluN2B protein expression. Collectively, these findings support hippocampus-targeted TIS as a promising non-invasive neuromodulation approach and provide preclinical evidence for its potential to alleviate recognition memory impairments in depression.
